segments.arabic: [819] حدثنا ابن المثنى قال: حدثني غندر قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: سمعت سليمان الشيباني قال: سمعت الشعبي قال:
segments.english: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Ghundar related to me. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard Sulayman al-Shaybani say: I heard al-Sha‘bi say:

segments.arabic: أخبرني من مر مع النبي ﷺ على قبر منبوذ فأمهم وصفوا عليه
segments.english: Someone who passed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by an isolated grave informed me that he led them in prayer and they formed rows at it.

segments.arabic: فقلت: يا أبا عمرو من حدثك، فقال ابن عباس
segments.english: I said, “Abu ‘Amr, who related this to you?” He said, “Ibn ‘Abbas.”

notes: The initially unnamed informant is identified only in the closing exchange. The selected at it is retained rather than importing behind him from another wording. The historical print expands Ibn al-Muthanna to Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and has related to us for Ghundar; the selected text and modern print have related to me. Classical commentary explains the vocalised isolated-grave reading and records an alternative genitive construction.

segments.arabic: [820] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثني صفوان بن سليم عن عطاء بن يسار عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Safwan ibn Sulaym related to me, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: الغسل يوم الجمعة واجب على كل محتلم
segments.english: Bathing on Friday is obligatory for everyone who has reached puberty.

notes: The wording is translated without adding Muslim from the Khan-family comparison or appending a legal explanation of obligatory.

segments.arabic: [821] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: أخبرنا سفيان عن عمرو قال: أخبرني كريب عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from ‘Amr, who said: Kurayb informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: بت عند خالتي ميمونة ليلة فنام النبي ﷺ فلما كان في بعض الليل قام رسول الله ﷺ فتوضأ من شن معلق وضوءا خفيفا
segments.english: One night I stayed with my maternal aunt Maymunah, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept. When part of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, got up and performed a light ablution from a hanging worn waterskin.

segments.arabic: يخففه عمرو ويقلله جدا
segments.english: ‘Amr described it as light and very small in amount.

segments.arabic: ثم قام يصلي فقمت فتوضأت نحوا مما توضأ ثم جئت فقمت عن يساره فحولني فجعلني عن يمينه ثم صلى ما شاء الله ثم اضطجع فنام حتى نفخ فأتاه المنادي يأذنه بالصلاة فقام معه إلى الصلاة فصلى ولم يتوضأ
segments.english: Then he stood to pray. I got up and performed ablution much as he had, then came and stood on his left. He moved me and placed me on his right. Then he prayed as much as Allah willed, then lay down and slept until he snored. The caller came and informed him of the prayer. He got up with him to go to the prayer, prayed, and did not perform ablution.

segments.arabic: قلنا لعمرو إن ناسا يقولون إن النبي ﷺ تنام عينه ولا ينام قلبه قال عمرو سمعت عبيد بن عمير يقول إن رؤيا الأنبياء وحي ثم قرأ { إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك }
segments.english: We said to ‘Amr, “Some people say that the eye of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sleeps, but his heart does not sleep.” ‘Amr said, “I heard ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr say: ‘The dreams of the prophets are revelation.’” Then he recited: {I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you.}

notes: The intermediate Amr description and complete closing exchange remain. Eye stays singular, and the Quran excerpt is limited to the selected words. Neither Fajr nor the last hours of the night is inserted. The historical print adds an honorific after prophets and has related to us for Sufyan; these are not imported into the selected text.

segments.arabic: [822] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن جدته مليكة دعت رسول الله ﷺ لطعام صنعته فأكل منه، فقال قوموا فلأصلي بكم فقمت إلى حصير لنا قد اسود من طول ما لبس فنضحته بماء فقام رسول الله ﷺ واليتيم معي والعجوز من ورائنا فصلى بنا ركعتين
segments.english: His grandmother Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to some food she had prepared. He ate some of it and said, “Get up so I may lead you in prayer.” I went to a mat of ours that had become black from long use and sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood. The orphan was with me and the old woman behind us. He led us in two rak‘ahs.

notes: The selected shift from his grandmother to I went remains. The source does not say here that he stood on the mat or place the orphan in the first row; these comparison expansions are not inserted. Both selected prophetic honorifics remain.

segments.arabic: [823] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: أقبلت راكبا على حمار أتان وأنا يومئذ قد ناهزت الاحتلام ورسول الله ﷺ يصلي بالناس بمنى إلى غير جدار فمررت بين يدي بعض الصف فنزلت وأرسلت الأتان ترتع ودخلت في الصف فلم ينكر ذلك علي أحد
segments.english: I approached riding a she-donkey. At that time I had nearly reached puberty, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was leading the people in prayer at Mina without a wall in front of him. I passed in front of part of the row, dismounted, let the she-donkey graze and entered the row. No one objected to what I had done.

notes: Nahaztu means approached or nearly reached, as Ibn Hajar explicitly explains. The past-puberty or already-attained wording in the two English comparisons is not imported. The explicit dismounting, people being led, and part of the row remain.

segments.arabic: [824] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير أن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: أعتم النبي ﷺ،
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed until late.

segments.arabic: وقال عياش حدثنا عبد الأعلى حدثنا معمر عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Ayyash said: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us. Ma‘mar related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: أعتم رسول الله ﷺ في العشاء حتى ناداه عمر قد نام النساء والصبيان فخرج رسول الله ﷺ، فقال إنه ليس أحد من أهل الأرض يصلي هذه الصلاة غيركم
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the night prayer until ‘Umar called to him, “The women and children have gone to sleep.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and said, “No one among the people of the earth is praying this prayer except you.”

segments.arabic: ولم يكن أحد يومئذ يصلي غير أهل المدينة
segments.english: At that time no one prayed except the people of Madinah.

notes: Both complete opening routes and the short first report remain; the Khan-family comparison supplies only the longer account. The historical print uses Messenger in the first report where the selected text and modern print use Prophet. The final place-and-time observation remains separate from the quoted speech.

segments.arabic: [825] حدثنا عمرو بن علي قال: حدثنا يحيى قال: حدثنا سفيان حدثني عبد الرحمن بن عابس سمعت ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abis related to me: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both.

segments.arabic: قال له رجل شهدت الخروج مع رسول الله ﷺ قال: نعم ولولا مكاني منه ما شهدته يعني من صغره أتى العلم الذي عند دار كثير بن الصلت ثم خطب ثم أتى النساء فوعظهن، وذكرهن وأمرهن أن يتصدقن فجعلت المرأة تهوي بيدها إلى حلقها تلقي في ثوب بلال ثم أتى هو وبلال البيت
segments.english: A man said to him, “Were you present when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out?” He said, “Yes. Had it not been for my position with him, I would not have been present”—meaning because of his youth. He came to the marker by the house of Kathir ibn al-Salt, then gave an address. Then he came to the women, admonished them, reminded them and instructed them to give charity. A woman would reach with her hand to her throat, dropping something into Bilal’s garment. Then he and Bilal came to the house.

notes: The youth explanation remains an aside with the selected third-person his. Eid, kinship, a necklace, the owner of the final house and an additional prophetic honorific are not supplied inside the source text. The modern print omits reminded them, while the selected text and historical print include it; the selected phrase remains.

segments.arabic: [826] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: أعتم رسول الله ﷺ بالعتمة حتى ناداه عمر نام النساء والصبيان فخرج النبي ﷺ، فقال: ما ينتظرها أحد غيركم من أهل الأرض
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the night prayer until ‘Umar called to him, “The women and children have gone to sleep.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and said, “No one among the people of the earth is waiting for it except you.”

segments.arabic: ولا يصلي يومئذ إلا بالمدينة وكانوا يصلون العتمة فيما بين أن يغيب الشفق إلى ثلث الليل الأول
segments.english: At that time prayer was performed only in Madinah. They used to pray the night prayer between the disappearance of twilight and the first third of the night.

notes: The waiting wording differs from the praying wording in 824 and is not harmonised. The final two observations stay outside the quoted speech. No extra night or an exact clock time is supplied.

segments.arabic: [827] حدثنا عبيد الله بن موسى عن حنظلة عن سالم بن عبد الله عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, from Hanzalah, from Salim ibn ‘Abdullah, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا استأذنكم نساؤكم بالليل إلى المسجد فأذنوا لهن
segments.english: When your women ask your permission at night to go to the mosque, give them permission.

segments.arabic: تابعه شعبة عن الأعمش عن مجاهد عن ابن عمر عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Shu‘bah corroborated it, from al-A‘mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The full corroborating route includes Shubah and al-Amash, not only Mujahid as in the abridged Bewley note. Both prophetic honorifics remain.

segments.arabic: [828] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد حدثنا عثمان بن عمر أخبرنا يونس عن الزهري قال: حدثتني هند بنت الحارث أن أم سلمة زوج النبي ﷺ أخبرتها
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar related to us. Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Hind bint al-Harith related to me that Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed her:

segments.arabic: أن النساء في عهد رسول الله ﷺ كن إذا سلمن من المكتوبة قمن وثبت رسول الله ﷺ ومن صلى من الرجال ما شاء الله فإذا قام رسول الله ﷺ قام الرجال
segments.english: In the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the women would rise when they had said the closing greeting of the obligatory prayer. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the men who had prayed remained as long as Allah willed. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose, the men rose.

notes: All four prophetic honorifics and the informed-her link remain. The historical print has Yunus related to us; the selected text and modern print have informed us.

segments.arabic: [829] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك ح
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik.

segments.arabic: وحدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن عمرة بنت عبد الرحمن عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: And ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: إن كان رسول الله ﷺ ليصلي الصبح فينصرف النساء متلفعات بمروطهن ما يعرفن من الغلس
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would indeed pray the dawn prayer, and the women would leave wrapped in their garments, unrecognisable in the darkness.

notes: The two opening routes and the shared Malik link remain. The Arabic chain-switch marker ح remains in its original source span; it is represented by separate chain sections, not spoken as a narrator name.

segments.arabic: [830] حدثنا محمد بن مسكين قال: حدثنا بشر أخبرنا الأوزاعي حدثني يحيى بن أبي كثير عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة الأنصارى عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Miskin related to us. He said: Bishr related to us. Al-Awza‘i informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to me, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah al-Ansari, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إني لأقوم إلى الصلاة وأنا أريد أن أطول فيها فأسمع بكاء الصبي فأتجوز في صلاتي كراهية أن أشق على أمه
segments.english: I stand to pray intending to make it long, but I hear a child crying and shorten my prayer, disliking to cause hardship to his mother.

notes: The father is Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah’s father; the Bewley comparison’s Abu Qatada’s father wording is not imported. The historical print expands Bishr to Bishr ibn Bakr and uses related to us for Yahya; the selected short name and related to me remain.

segments.arabic: [831] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن عمرة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: لو أدرك رسول الله ﷺ ما أحدث النساء لمنعهن كما منعت نساء بني إسرائيل
segments.english: Had the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seen what the women had introduced, he would have prevented them, as the women of the Children of Israel were prevented.

segments.arabic: قلت لعمرة أو منعن قالت نعم
segments.english: I asked ‘Amrah, “Were they prevented?” She said, “Yes.”

notes: The selected wording concerns what women had introduced, not a prediction of what they would do. The selected text and modern print do not contain the historical print’s explicit mosque object after prevented them; that expansion is not imported. The closing I asked is not replaced with an added narrator name.

segments.arabic: [832] حدثنا يحيى بن قزعة قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن الزهري عن هند بنت الحارث عن أم سلمة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Yahya ibn Qaza‘ah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Hind bint al-Harith, from Umm Salamah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا سلم قام النساء حين يقضي تسليمه ويمكث هو في مقامه يسيرا قبل أن يقوم
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said the closing greeting, the women would rise as soon as he finished saying it. He would remain in his place a little while before rising.

segments.arabic: قال نرى والله أعلم أن ذلك كان لكي ينصرف النساء قبل أن يدركهن أحد من الرجال
segments.english: He said: We think—and Allah knows best—that this was so the women could leave before any of the men caught up with them.

notes: We think remains plural, unlike I think in the Bewley comparison. The selected final any of the men remains; the historical print omits the explicit any. The narrator is not named inside this selected closing phrase.

segments.arabic: [833] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا ابن عيينة عن إسحاق عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from Ishaq, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ في بيت أم سليم فقمت ويتيم خلفه وأم سليم خلفنا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in the house of Umm Sulaym. An orphan and I stood behind him, and Umm Sulaym stood behind us.

notes: The selected short Ibn Uyaynah, Ishaq and Anas names remain where the historical print expands them. The source’s unspecified orphan is not assigned a name. The modern print repeats a related version as 874 after 835; that separate tail occurrence is recorded in the boundary audit, not silently deduplicated into this entry.

segments.arabic: [834] حدثنا يحيى بن موسى حدثنا سعيد بن منصور حدثنا فليح عن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Yahya ibn Musa related to us. Sa‘id ibn Mansur related to us. Fulayh related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يصلي الصبح بغلس فينصرفن نساء المؤمنين لا يعرفن من الغلس أو لا يعرفن بعضهن بعضا
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the dawn prayer in the darkness. The women of the believers would leave, unrecognisable because of the darkness, or they would not recognise one another.

notes: The alternative OR is explicit and is not replaced with NOR as in Bewley. The source’s women of the believers wording remains. No Arabic character is normalised, including the selected written plural ending.

segments.arabic: [835] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا يزيد بن زريع عن معمر عن الزهري عن سالم بن عبد الله عن أبيه عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim ibn ‘Abdullah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

segments.arabic: إذا استأذنت امرأة أحدكم فلا يمنعها
segments.english: If the wife of any of you asks permission, he must not prevent her.

notes: The selected text and both Arabic prints lack an at-night qualification and an explicit mosque object in this report. The Bewley entry repeats the expanded wording of 827; it is recorded as a comparison difference, not imported. The Khan-family comparison places to go to the mosque in parentheses; those words are not inserted.

The modern Arabic print continues with two further numbered occurrences, 874 and 875, under a repeated Women praying behind men heading. The selected digital section and historical print end here. Those occurrences are logged separately for edition-coverage review; they are neither merged into 832/833 nor claimed as admitted.
